big_case.notes: First district court preliminary injunction blocking IIRIRA section 102(c) border-barrier waivers in two decades, halting construction across the 517-mile Big Bend Sector (including Big Bend National Park) under the $46.5B OBBBA appropriation, and eliciting a published per curiam Supreme Court opinion holding under Dalton v. Specter, Biden v. Nebraska, and FCC v. Consumers' Research that there is no such thing as a 'constitutional' major-questions claim within section 102(c)(2)(A)'s jurisdiction-stripping exception.

central_claims.basis: On November 9, 2026, the Court granted the application for stay pending the filing and disposition of a timely petition for a writ of certiorari and declined to summarily reverse.
central_claims.claim: The Court will grant an unqualified stay of the Western District of Texas preliminary injunction pending the filing and disposition of a timely certiorari petition, rather than granting summary reversal.

central_claims.basis: On November 9, 2026, Justice Alito referred Application 26A560 to the full Court, which then granted the stay.
central_claims.claim: Justice Alito will refer the application to the full Court prior to disposition.

central_claims.basis: The per curiam opinion (writings/OT2026-2/01-per-curiam.txt) held that the Government is exceedingly likely to prevail because IIRIRA section 102(c)(2)(A) limits district court jurisdiction to constitutional claims, respondents' major-questions claim alleges only that the Secretary exceeded statutory authority under Dalton v. Specter, and 'there is no such thing as a 'constitutional' major-questions claim,' while also crediting border-security and nonrecoverable contractor-cost equities.
central_claims.claim: If the Court explains a grant, it will rely on the IIRIRA section 102(c)(2)(A) jurisdictional bar distinguishing a statutory major-questions challenge to the 'high illegal entry' predicate from a constitutional claim, alongside the government's border-security and construction-disruption equities.

central_claims.basis: No further response request occurred and no additional amicus briefs were filed after FAIR's October 29 brief (`outcome.interim_signals`: `response_requested: true`, `amicus_briefs: 1`), and the Court resolved the application on November 9, 2026 (11 days after October 29) after the Government filed its reply on October 30.
central_claims.claim: No additional response request or amicus filing will occur beyond the single amicus brief on the frozen record, and the order will issue within roughly one to two weeks after October 29 following a government reply.

central_claims.basis: The Court issued a 5-page per curiam opinion and Justice Jackson noted she would deny the application for stay without authoring a separate dissenting opinion (`writings.json` records only `01-per-curiam.txt`).
central_claims.claim: A short order is the leading route and a reasoned dissent is plausible (with Justices Jackson and Sotomayor as the likeliest individual writers), though an order with noted votes and no separate dissent remains quite possible.
